subject: Food Science
title: Canning and Retort
description: A fast breakdown of Canning and Retort for builders.

hook.text: Napoleon offered 12,000 francs to anyone who could preserve food for his army.

buildup.text: Canning seals food in airtight containers, then heats to 121°C to destroy all microorganisms.

discovery.text: Retort processing uses pressurized steam to heat cans above water's boiling point.

twist.text: Canned food can last 5+ years. In 1974, cans from a steamboat sunk in 1865 were opened.

climax.text: Canning and Retort matters because clearer reasoning leads to better judgments.

punchline.text: Seal it. Heat it. Kill everything. Canning made food last years.

quiz.question: Why must canning achieve 121°C?
options: To destroy heat-resistant Clostridium botulinum spores
